work_order.understanding: Six non-blocking review findings from PR #60 (merged as dff184c). Five still reproduce verbatim on main and are fixed here; the sixth (PR #60's title lacks the mandatory `[AI]` prefix) is dropped, because that PR is merged and its squash subject `fix: Follow-ups from #48: 7 from the review (#60)` is already on main — retitelling the PR cannot change the commit, and this ticket must not rewrite published history. All five live changes are internal to two e2e files plus one release-note front-matter key; nothing under packages/*/src changes, so no user-visible behaviour moves. The shared theme is PR #60's own stated principle — a channel that stops delivering, or a comment that claims more than the code checks, must fail on every run — applied consistently to the sibling file and to the comments it left. Concretely: (1) command-bar.test.ts:132 claims each regex alternative has *its own* probe while the assertion above it only proves each has *at least one* matching probe; (2) reports.test.ts:272 drains the pageerror channel with a bare waitForTimeout and asserts it is empty, with nothing proving the channel still delivers — the exact vacuous-pass hole PR #60 closed in its own file, left open in the sibling file PR #60 edits; (3) the DIALOG_WARNING_PROBES doc block (lines 40-41) and the inline block above the probe (lines 148-150) state the probe's property near-verbatim, 108 lines apart; (4) CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS now backs two waits with different meanings while its doc names one; (5) the release note is categorised Bugfix for a diff that touches no production code.
work_order.root_cause: PR #60 added a self-checking probe to the file it was about (command-bar.test.ts) and left two seams unclosed: the sibling file that shares the same channel-assertion shape (reports.test.ts), and its own file's comments and constants, which were extended past what they were written to describe. Nothing here is a product defect; it is a test-hardening change whose own documentation drifted from its code.
work_order.approach: Four edits across two e2e files and one release note, plus one documented drop. (a) In reports.test.ts, give the pageerror channel the same self-check command-bar.test.ts already has: keep `expect(pageErrors).toEqual([])` where it is, and immediately after it attach a *second* `page.on('pageerror')` collector, throw once from inside the page via `page.evaluate(() => { setTimeout(() => { throw new Error('probe') }, 0) })`, and `await expect.poll(() => probeErrors.length, { timeout: PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS }).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. Order is load-bearing and mirrors command-bar.test.ts:146-147 — the throw must come after the emptiness assertion or it poisons the buffer it is meant to be independent of. (b) In command-bar.test.ts, reword the coverage comment at :132 to state what `.some()` actually enforces (at least one matching probe per alternative) instead of the stronger bijection it does not enforce, and delete the duplicated 'They are emitted from the page by the probe below so every run re-proves that both channels deliver and the filter still matches the transcribed wording.' sentence from the DIALOG_WARNING_PROBES doc block — the transcription-drift caveat immediately above it already covers what only that block knows. (c) In the same file, give the probe's `expect.poll` its own constant, PROBE_SETTLE_MS, documented as the probe's deadline, leaving CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS documented as and used only for the drain. (d) Re-categorise upcoming-release-notes/fix-command-bar-dialog-console-drain.md from Bugfix to Maintenance, which is also this PR's own release note and satisfies the release-notes gate. No new helper is extracted: watchDialogWarnings is console-channel-and-filter specific and has exactly one caller, so a shared pageerror helper would have one caller too.

files.change: In `test('creates a custom report in an empty budget')`, keep lines 246-247 (`const pageErrors: Error[] = []` / `page.on('pageerror', error => pageErrors.push(error))`) and lines 272-273 (`await page.waitForTimeout(PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS);` / `expect(pageErrors).toEqual([]);`) exactly as they are. Immediately after `expect(pageErrors).toEqual([])` and before the closing `});` of the test, add a self-check that proves the pageerror channel still delivers, mirroring command-bar.test.ts:155-167: `const probeErrors: Error[] = [];` then `page.on('pageerror', error => probeErrors.push(error));` (a SECOND collector — do not reuse pageErrors), then `await page.evaluate(() => { setTimeout(() => { throw new Error('pageerror probe') }, 0); });`, then `await expect.poll(() => probeErrors.length, { timeout: PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS }).toBeGreaterThan(0);`. The `setTimeout` wrapper is required: throwing synchronously inside page.evaluate rejects the evaluate call instead of surfacing as an uncaught page error. Add a comment above the block, in the voice of the existing ones, stating (1) it must stay after the emptiness assertion because the throw is a real page error and would fail it, (2) it proves the channel delivers into a collector within PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS so a channel that stops delivering turns this test red on every run instead of passing vacuously, and (3) it does NOT prove the app is free of page errors — only that the channel works.
files.why: The single finding with real code in it, and the one the route note names as the reason QA stays. `grep -rn 'probe\|evaluate\|poll' reports.test.ts` shows the only `poll` uses are chart-scroll geometry at 197-211 — nothing near line 272 self-checks the channel, so `expect(pageErrors).toEqual([])` still passes vacuously if pageerror stops delivering.

files.change: Three edits. (1) Coverage comment at line 132: change the first sentence from `// Every alternative in the filter needs its own probe, or the arm nobody` `// probes is a blind spot:` to `// Every alternative in the filter needs a probe that matches it, or the` `// arm nobody probes is a blind spot:` — dropping `its own`, which is the bijection the `.some()` below does not enforce. Leave the rest of that comment block (the blind-spot rationale, and the note that the naive `split('|')` is correct only for a flat alternation) as it is; the assertion itself at lines 137-144 is NOT changed. (2) DIALOG_WARNING_PROBES doc block: delete the trailing two lines ` * the page by the probe below so every run re-proves that both channels deliver` ` * and the filter still matches the transcribed wording.` and rewrite the sentence they complete (`These are held as literals rather than read out of the installed package, so they can rot if a patch release rewords either message.`) so the block ends there. The block keeps the channel mapping and the first-line-only truncation note; the full claim about what the probe proves stays in the inline block at 146-154, which is what a reader hits while debugging. (3) Constants: after `const CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS = 1000;` at line 24 add `/** How long the probe's expect.poll waits for the emitted warnings to arrive. */` `const PROBE_SETTLE_MS = 1000;` (same value, so no runtime change today), and change the poll timeout at line 166 from `{ timeout: CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS }` to `{ timeout: PROBE_SETTLE_MS }`. Line 125, the drain, keeps CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS.
files.why: Findings 1, 3 and 4. After the edit, `grep -n 'filter still matches' command-bar.test.ts` returns exactly one line, and `grep -n CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS` returns the declaration, its doc, and the drain at 125 — not the poll.

files.change: Change the front-matter `category: Bugfix` to `category: Maintenance`. Leave `authors: [Shivam-Fl]` and the one-line body unchanged.

Editing this note also satisfies the release-notes gate, which requires an added-or-modified note under upcoming-release-notes/ on every PR.

risks: The reports.test.ts probe deliberately throws inside the page. If it were ever moved above the emptiness assertion it would turn the test red permanently — the ordering is the one thing a future edit can silently break, which is why AC-2 pins it.

PROBE_SETTLE_MS is introduced at the same 1000ms value as CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS, so no test runtime changes today; the risk is future, that someone tunes the drain down for speed and is surprised the probe no longer follows — hence the two separately documented constants.

Rewording the coverage comment (AC-3) weakens no guard but makes the file's stated property slightly less ambitious than the comment previously read. If a future reader wants the bijection enforced, that is a real follow-up, not something this change half-does.
No file under packages/*/src is touched and no host is added to env.api_allowlist, so neither the forbidden-paths gate nor the network allowlist should stop QA.
The dropped finding (retitling merged PR #60) cannot be fixed from here and its squash subject is already published on main. This PR's own title must carry the `[AI]` prefix itself.

Rewriting published main history is not this ticket's job. The `[AI]` rule is honoured forward: this PR's title carries the prefix.

Enforcing the one-probe-per-alternative bijection in the coverage assertion (asserting exactly one matching probe per alternative instead of rewording the comment). The reviewer's own evidence shows this is not a live blind spot — narrowing either alternative still fails `.some()` — and a strict-count assertion would make the test fail on a future broadening that is harmless. Recorded as TR-2's cheaper alternative, not taken.

Extracting a shared `watchPageErrors` helper alongside `watchDialogWarnings`. The two differ in channel (pageerror vs console) and in filtering (none vs a regex), and each would have exactly one caller, so the abstraction would exist for its own sake.

Rewriting the command-bar.test.ts screenshot snapshots or touching any other e2e file. `grep -rn "page.on(" packages/desktop-client/e2e/` returns only command-bar.test.ts:75 and reports.test.ts:247, which is the complete blast radius of this finding.
Backporting `PROBE_SETTLE_MS` to PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS in reports.test.ts — that constant already backs exactly one wait, so there is nothing to split.

work_order.confidence_rationale: Every code finding was verified by reading the exact cited lines on main rather than trusting the issue's reproduction, and each edit is a comment, a constant, or one mirrored probe block — no behaviour of the app changes and no new abstraction is introduced. The main residual uncertainty is mechanical: `expect.poll` on the pageerror channel in reports.test.ts has not been executed here, and the release-notes gate's acceptance of a modified note is inferred from the script's diff-filter and two prior commits rather than read off a green CI run. Confidence is below 90 for that reason.
